text: {"overall_winner":"A","qualities":[{"evidence":"“The positives to driverless cars do not outweight those of the negatives” and repeated “I believe” statements","quality":"clear stance","description":"The essay states its position early and keeps that opposition to driverless cars explicit throughout."},{"evidence":"paragraphs on cost, carelessness, and faulty machines","quality":"argument development","description":"It develops multiple reasons in separate body paragraphs instead of relying on one main point."},{"evidence":"“This would not change the fact...” and “People are not perfect, and althought...”","quality":"counterargument handling","description":"It acknowledges possible benefits and objections before explaining why the negatives still matter more."},{"evidence":"“The United States alone is nineteen-billion dollars in debt... even if we wanted to make driverless cars in mass bulk”","quality":"reasoning depth","description":"It offers more extended explanation for why a claim matters rather than only restating a concern."},{"evidence":"conclusion that revisits cost, safety, and the broader impact on the industry","quality":"concluding synthesis","description":"It closes by tying together several points into a broader final judgment instead of simply repeating earlier claims."}]}
